findings.evidence: a technical proposal ("add Kafka") is not evidence of business value. Ask the user only what code cannot reveal: users, policy, priorities, trade-offs, success measures.
findings.fix: Cut the general product-management advice the model already knows. Keep only the specific instruction: "Ask whether an existing capability or a smaller change solves the problem; ask the user only for users, policy, priorities, trade-offs and success measures."

findings.evidence: Ask the 2–3 questions whose answers could change scope, an irreversible decision, or an acceptance test
findings.fix: Add a tie-break for when more than three questions qualify: irreversible decisions first (data retention, permissions, public APIs), then the category with the lowest score relative to its maximum, then questions that unblock the most acceptance criteria.

findings.evidence: Gotchas cover sub-90 drafts, padding, overwrites and failed saves, but not a user who hands a choice back ("you decide", "whatever's standard")
findings.fix: Add this gotcha: "When the user says 'you decide', log your proposal as an assumption with the user as owner. Never log it as a decision or turn it into an acceptance criterion, because nobody signed off on it and it will be challenged in review."

findings.evidence: Assertions in vague-login and clarified-spec are not verifiable: "Identifies missing auth/context decisions", "Does not invent answers or generate finished PRD"; these first three evals also have no input files.
findings.fix: Replace each with a checkable assertion, for example "Asks about at least one of: sign-in method (password, SSO, magic link), account recovery, or who can sign up" and "Shows no stack, metric or deadline that the prompt does not contain".

findings.evidence: Repeat still-open questions each round; users tend to answer only the latest ones.
findings.fix: Add a stop rule for when the score stalls below 90 or the user stops answering: "After 3 rounds with less than 10 points gained, or after a round with no answers, offer a draft PRD with every open item listed under open questions, instead of asking another round."

findings.evidence: 'Find out which user problem the request solves and whether an existing capability or smaller change would solve it' is standard requirements-elicitation advice. By section length, Route first (7 lines) is mainly activation; Workflow (20 lines) mixes custom protocol with familiar engineering advice; Clarity rubric (18 lines) supplies the strongest custom framework; Gotchas (6 lines) mixes concrete repository conventions with familiar reminders.
findings.fix: Compress step 2 to the consequential product decisions repository inspection cannot establish. Retain the ambiguous-path routing examples, custom scoring rules, decision provenance and conflict handling; those add more knowledge than the general explanation of business value and smaller alternatives.

findings.evidence: 'Ask the 2–3 questions' is reinforced by 'the next 2–3 questions' at line 53, without an exception when only one consequential decision remains unresolved.
findings.fix: Change both instructions to ask up to three focused questions, explicitly allowing a single question when only one consequential gap remains. Preserve the one-decision-per-question rule.

findings.evidence: 'Footer has Document version 1.0, Created 2026-11-03' fixes the document creation date to the attached notes' session date, but the test prompt does not pin the current date. A correct PRD generated on another day could fail this assertion.
findings.fix: Explicitly supply 2026-11-03 as the document creation date in the test prompt or freeze the evaluation date. Alternatively, assert that Created matches the evaluation's supplied current date and keep the historical clarification-session date separate.
